data.name: Body.MainExplanation.Lead
data.value: Overbodige bestanden hieronder zijn [veilig te verwijderen].
data.comment: Main window intro, key 1 of 3 (the lead). Rendered prominent (heading tier): the reassurance the window opens on. "Any" and not "The": the same sentence shows over a count of zero, so it must read correctly with no files below it. Keep it one short clause. The bracketed phrase becomes a hyperlink into the README's "Is it safe?" section (rendered in MainWindow.xaml.cs BuildIntroLeadLine); the brackets are the delimiter and are not shown. This is the screen's strongest safety claim and the only link on it, so keep the brackets on whatever phrase carries that claim in this language.

data.name: Body.MainExplanation.Why
data.value: Ze staan in {InstallerFolder}. InstallerClean vraagt Windows naar elk geïnstalleerd programma: een bestand komt in de lijst wanneer geen enkel programma het opeist ({0}), of wanneer een nieuwere patch het heeft vervangen en geen enkel programma erop kan terugvallen ({1}).
data.comment: Main window intro, key 2 of 3 (the why, rendered muted). TWO PLACEHOLDERS, ONE PER CAUSE THE OFFER CAN CONTAIN: {0} is Reason.Orphaned and {1} is Reason.Superseded, the only two labels the scan sets (FileSystemScanService, the walked-file branch and the superseded-patch branch). Reason.Obsoleted is still passed as {2} by MainViewModel and is deliberately unused here: an obsoleted registration is counted at scan time and never offered, so naming that cause on this screen would describe a file the list cannot hold. Carrying the labels as placeholders means a translator edits each one in a single place and this sentence follows. THE OPENING CLAUSE CARRIES THE EPISTEMICS FOR BOTH HALVES: it says what the app asked, so what follows is read as the answer it got and not as an assertion about the machine. IT PARTITIONS BECAUSE THE SET HAS TWO CAUSES, and a sentence naming one of them is false of the other half: an orphan is offered because no registration claims its file, and a superseded patch is offered BECAUSE a registration does claim it and reports the patch replaced. THE SECOND CLAUSE'S ROLLBACK HALF IS NOT A RESTATEMENT OF ITS FIRST and must not be dropped as one in any language: replaced is not finished with, since uninstalling whatever replaced the patch can roll back onto it and reach for this exact file, which is the condition that decides whether a superseded patch is offered at all. The single-cause sentence this replaces was true only while the superseded class was withheld, which is a state no released version was ever in. BOTH CLAUSES ARE ABOUT THE ANSWER THE APP RECEIVED AND NOT ABOUT THE STATE OF THE MACHINE, which is the weaker claim and the one that stays true whatever an enumeration cannot see, so it is kept rather than tightened. The wording this replaces gave two reasons for that framing and neither survives at 3.0.0: the instance-code reading lost its subject once nothing read inside a cached file any more (see InstanceProductCount, which says so in its own words), and a recorded path spelled in a form the folder walk never produces is expanded and handled from 3.0.0 rather than guarded against (see NormaliseLocalPackagePath). The framing outlives its old reasons. Translations must keep both clauses statements about what came back; a rendering that says outright that Windows has no record of the file makes a claim about the machine that this wording exists to avoid.

data.name: Body.MainExplanation.Action
data.value: Move them to a backup folder you choose, then delete that folder when you're satisfied your programs still update and uninstall as normal. If anything does go wrong, put them back into {InstallerFolder} under the names they had. Or delete them permanently now.
data.comment: Main window intro, key 3 of 3 (the action, rendered in the body tier). MOVE IS NAMED FIRST AND DELETE LAST, REVERSING WHAT THIS LINE USED TO DO, and the reason is not doubt about the offer: the lead above says these files are safe to delete and that claim stands at full strength. It is that Move is the only route by which a person can satisfy themselves, and the app had never told anybody how, leaving a real user to work it out for himself and say so in public. THE MIDDLE CLAUSE IS THE WHOLE OF THAT INSTRUCTION AND BOTH OPERATIONS ARE NAMED ON PURPOSE: update and uninstall are what a cached package is kept for, so somebody who has done both and seen nothing break has exercised the thing the file exists for. Naming fewer leaves a person guessing what else to try. REPAIR WAS THE THIRD AND CAME OUT ON A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN ON CAUTION. A repair does not read the cached file: on one real machine seven of eight products failed a repair with the file present and one succeeded with it absent. So the check established nothing about what this app had done, and it fails often for reasons that predate the app entirely. Somebody following the old instruction, meeting a failed repair and concluding InstallerClean had broken their machine, is the worst thing this sentence could have produced. "Then delete that folder" is the finish and must survive translation: without it the advice is to move files somewhere and keep them for ever, which reclaims nothing and is not what Move is for. THE THIRD SENTENCE IS AN INSTRUCTION AND NOT A PROMISE, WHICH IS A CORRECTION RATHER THAN A HEDGE. It read "Putting them back into {InstallerFolder} restores everything", and that is false of a move whose destination already held a file of the same name: MoveFilesService.GetUniqueDestPath renames a colliding name.msi to name (1).msi and no surface anywhere says so, so a user who follows the old sentence and puts THAT back has restored nothing. A cached package counts as present if and only if its recorded LocalPackage path exists, so the name is the whole of what makes a restore work, and "under the names they had" covers the renamed case without making anybody read about the rename. Keep the folder named rather than "back where they were": it is the whole instruction, and it is the one thing the window never said before. NO QUALIFIER BELONGS ON THIS LINE, and a draft carrying one was rejected rather than never written. It would have sat three lines under the safe-to-delete claim and argued with it, and attaching it to Delete alone would imply Move protects against something the app declines to name, which is the shape a rival would have chosen. The screen's safety claim is ONE decision across the lead and this line and not two: anything that hedged here would have had to weaken the lead in the same pass. The limit is stated once, in the README, which the bracketed phrase in the lead links to. The button order is a separate matter and does not govern this line.

data.name: Body.RegisteredMissingFromDisk
data.value:
This installer file is missing. It causes no trouble now, and won't until the day you try to update or uninstall the program it belongs to. That step can then fail, because Windows looks for this file and it isn't there.
To put it back, you need the installer for the version you already have. Get it from the program's maker and run it over your existing copy. A newer version won't do: it has to remove the one you've got first, and that's the step that needs this file. Uninstalling first won't work either, for the same reason. This should restore the file and leave your settings alone, but Microsoft doesn't guarantee it.
data.comment: Shown in the Registered Files details pane when a selected product's installer file is gone from disk. Generic with no product name interpolated: the recovery advice is identical for every program, and a possessive on a name ending in s reads wrongly.

data.name: Error.AdminRequiredBody
data.value:
Windows heeft InstallerClean de toegang geweigerd, dus het is gestopt. Er is niets verwijderd.
InstallerClean draaide al als administrator, dus opnieuw starten op die manier helpt niet. Windows zegt er niet bij wat er precies weigerde, dus er valt niets gerichts te proberen.

data.name: Error.InstallerDbUnavailableTitle
data.value: Windows Installer-records konden niet worden gelezen

data.name: Error.InstallerDbEmpty
data.value: De Windows Installer-records kwamen volledig leeg terug: geen enkel geïnstalleerd programma of geen enkele update maakt aanspraak op een installatiebestand in de cache. Dat komt op een werkende computer niet voor (zelfs een gloednieuwe Windows-installatie heeft er een paar), dus ofwel zijn de records beschadigd, ofwel konden ze niet worden gelezen, en een scan die dit antwoord zou geloven, zou elk bestand in {InstallerFolder} ten onrechte verweesd noemen. InstallerClean is in plaats daarvan gestopt. Er is niets verwijderd.

data.name: Error.MsiAccessDenied
data.value: Windows Installer weigerde InstallerClean te laten zien wat er geïnstalleerd is. InstallerClean draaide al als administrator, dus het nogmaals als administrator uitvoeren verandert niets. Zonder die lijst is er geen veilige manier om te bepalen welke bestanden in de cache nog nodig zijn, dus InstallerClean is gestopt. Er is niets verwijderd.

data.name: Error.MsiNonSuccess
data.value: Windows Installer kon InstallerClean geen leesbare lijst van de geïnstalleerde programma's geven: {0} vermeldingen op rij kwamen onleesbaar terug (laatste foutcode {1}). In plaats van met een half gelezen lijst te werken is InstallerClean gestopt. Er is niets verwijderd.

data.name: Error.MsiEnumerationNeverEnded
data.value: Windows Installer heeft het einde van de lijst met geïnstalleerde programma's nooit gemeld: InstallerClean heeft het na {0} vermeldingen opgegeven (laatste foutcode {1}). Een lijst zonder einde is niet te vertrouwen, dus InstallerClean is gestopt. Er is niets verwijderd.

data.name: Error.MsiPatchEnumerationNeverEnded
data.value: Windows Installer heeft het einde van de patchlijst van één programma nooit gemeld: InstallerClean heeft het na {0} vermeldingen opgegeven (laatste foutcode {1}). Een lijst zonder einde is niet te vertrouwen, dus InstallerClean is gestopt. Er is niets verwijderd.

data.name: Error.ScanCorrelationFailed
data.value: InstallerClean kon de Windows Installer-records niet koppelen aan de inhoud van {InstallerFolder}. Bijna niets waarnaar de records verwijzen staat daar werkelijk, en bijna niets van wat daar staat wordt door een record genoemd, waardoor er niets als overbodig kon worden aangemerkt. Er is niets voor opruimen aangeboden en er is niets verwijderd.

data.name: Error.ScanNoRegisteredFileInFolder
data.value: InstallerClean kon de Windows Installer-records niet koppelen aan de inhoud van {InstallerFolder}. De map bevat wel bestanden, maar geen enkel record verwijst naar iets daarin, waardoor er niets als overbodig kon worden aangemerkt. Er is niets voor opruimen aangeboden en er is niets verwijderd.

data.name: Error.ScanRecordsUnreadable
data.value: InstallerClean kon niet genoeg van de Windows Installer-records lezen om zeker te weten wat er nog nodig is: de lijst met geïnstalleerde programma's kwam onvolledig terug, en dezelfde records rechtstreeks uit het register lezen leverde ook fouten op. Een bestand kon er verweesd uitzien enkel doordat het record dat het benoemt een van de onleesbare was, dus InstallerClean is gestopt. Er is niets verwijderd.

data.name: Error.ScanCacheRootUnresolved
data.value: InstallerClean kreeg Windows niet zover het echte pad van {InstallerFolder} te bepalen, dus van geen enkel bestand kon worden aangetoond dat het erin staat en er is niets voor opruimen aangeboden. Deze scan vond niets omdat die controle mislukte, niet omdat de map schoon is. Er is niets verwijderd.

data.name: Error.InstallerLockUnavailable
data.value: InstallerClean kon de vergrendeling niet krijgen waarmee Windows Installer voorkomt dat twee programma's tegelijk geïnstalleerde software wijzigen, en kon dus niet uitsluiten dat een bestand halverwege alsnog nodig werd, dus er is niets verwijderd. Probeer het opnieuw, en herstart Windows als het zich blijft voordoen.
